description: Together, we are not just a team—we are explorers, and future changemakers!
summary:
What we developed:
We developed Black Box Doctor, an offline-first, professional medical cockpit software for spacecraft designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Built as a streamlined single-file prototype, it features a 3-tab user interface (Airlock Command Hub, Psych & Sleep Check-In, and Digital Twin Simulator), live autonomous physiological sliders with second-by-second micro-fluctuations, and an automated medical report PDF generator.

How it addresses the challenge:
The software directly solves the "Distance from Earth" and "Isolation" hazards of human spaceflight. During deep-space communication blackouts where Earth contact is severed and real-time medical support is impossible, Black Box Doctor operates entirely offline. It monitors vital health indicators against NASA standards, triggers instant anomaly warnings paired with verified NASA resources, and initiates automated MedKit locker routing for countermeasure dispensing.

Why it is important:
As space missions venture further into cislunar space and Mars, crews must manage medical emergencies autonomously. Black Box Doctor bridges communication gaps, protects astronaut survival, and ensures reliable, evidence-based health telemetry monitoring without relying on ground control.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

Black Box Doctor is a professional, offline-first medical cockpit designed specifically for spacecraft environments. It tracks and simulates critical astronaut health indicators—such as heart rate, blood pressure, stress levels, radiation exposure, sleep accumulation, and core temperature—using live, interactive sliders with autonomous second-by-second micro-fluctuations.

The Architecture: The app features a streamlined 3-tab layout: the Airlock Command Hub for real-time telemetry and anomaly alerts, the Psych & Sleep Check-In for mood tracking and neuro-cognitive reaction tests, and the Digital Twin Simulator for monitoring microgravity fluid shifts (including intracranial pressure and SANS risks).

Automated Safeguards: When vital thresholds are crossed, the system immediately triggers visual anomaly warnings, pairs them with verified NASA reference standards (like NASA-STD-3001), and initiates automated MedKit locker routing for countermeasure dispensing. It also allows crews to export session data into a downloadable PDF medical report.

2. What benefits does it have?

100% Offline Autonomy: Functions entirely without internet connectivity, cloud servers, or API keys, ensuring zero downtime during deep-space communication blackouts.

Instant Clarity: Built with an intuitive, cinematic HUD interface designed for rapid comprehension by anyone from a first grader to a mission commander.

Comprehensive Hazard Coverage: Unifies monitoring for all five hazards of human spaceflight (Radiation, Isolation/Confinement, Distance from Earth, Altered Gravity, and Hostile Environments) into a single dashboard.

Portable Design: Lightweight and built for local hardware deployment, including suit-mounted wrist access.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The project aims to protect astronaut survival during long-duration deep-space missions (such as Mars transit or cislunar travel) where real-time medical support from Earth is impossible due to severe communication delays. By bridging communication gaps and automating medical triage, Black Box Doctor empowers crews to manage health emergencies independently.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Languages & Frameworks: HTML5, Tailwind CSS, and JavaScript for user interface and core logic.

Platforms: Base44 for rapid deployment alongside a self-contained offline HTML build.

Reporting: Client-side libraries for generating professional PDF mission medical reports.

Hardware Context: Optimized for local spacecraft hardware storage and spacesuit integration.

5. How is your project creative?

Black Box Doctor transforms complex aerospace medicine into an immersive, high-stakes interactive spacecraft cockpit rather than a traditional spreadsheet or clinical monitor. By integrating real-time microgravity fluid-shift simulations (Digital Twin) with automated physical MedKit routing and offline reliability, it turns telemetry monitoring into an engaging, practical survival tool.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Reliability: Ensuring the software operates entirely offline without vulnerable API keys or cloud dependencies during live judging or actual space missions.

Scientific Rigor: Grounding every alert and metric strictly in official NASA standards (NASA-STD-3001, Human Research Roadmap, CCMC DONKI) with verified reference links.

Temporal Accuracy: Replacing Earth-bound time formats with Mission Elapsed Time (MET) and orbital status tracking.

Usability: Maintaining an intuitive, glanceable layout backed by professional documentation and presentation workflows.
